So motion, mover and And route are non-existent."},"philosophy":{"insight":"The chapter's devastating conclusion: neither entities nor non-entities can move in any of the three ways. Therefore ALL THREE elements — motion, mover, AND the route (path) — lack inherent existence. The entire framework of motion is empty. But this emptiness IS what makes conventional motion possible.","madhyamaka":"Garfield: \"non-existent\" (avidyamāna) means lacking svabhāva, NOT conventionally non-existent. Motion happens — people walk, cars drive — but none of these have inherent existence. Kalupahana: the addition of \"route\" (adhvan) is significant — even the PATH of motion is empty, completing the trinity of agent, action, and locus. Candrakīrti: this verse is the mahāsiddhi (great accomplishment) of Ch. 2 — the complete demonstration that motion in all its aspects is empty.","quantum":"Emergent Actuality / Contextual Properties: Quantum properties don't pre-exist measurement — they emerge contextually. Position, momentum, spin are not \"there\" waiting to be found; they arise through interaction with measurement apparatus. All three elements of quantum measurement (system, property, apparatus) are relationally constituted, not inherently fixed.","bridge":"Both show that the complete framework is relationally constituted. In quantum mechanics: system, property, and measurement context are all interdependent. In Madhyamaka: mover, motion, and route are all interdependent. Neither framework supports inherent, independent existence of any element. Both point to relational, dependent reality.","accessible":"A dance needs a dancer, dancing, and a dance floor. But none of these \"inherently exist\" — the dancer is only a dancer when dancing, the dancing only exists with a dancer, and the floor is only a dance floor when someone dances on it. All three arise together, dependently. That's Nāgārjuna's conclusion: motion, mover, and path are all empty — and that emptiness is what allows the dance to happen.","twoTruths":"Conventionally, motion is perfectly real and functional. Ultimately, the entire analysis shows motion, mover, and path lack inherent existence — they arise dependently and are empty.","commonMisconception":"The chapter's conclusion is NOT that motion is an illusion. Nothing in the motion-framework has inherent existence.","realLifeExample":"A road is only a \"road\" because people drive on it.
